entries.question: Where do I find the racks I scanned earlier? I can't find a History screen.
entries.answer:
Past scans live on your Profile screen, not on a separate History screen.

1. Tap PROFILE in the bottom bar (the person icon, third tab).
2. Scroll to the "Recent Scans" section.
3. Tap any row to reopen that scan's results.

On a desktop or iPad, click "Profile" in the left sidebar — its subtitle is "Account & history".

If you saved an old /history bookmark, it still works: RackTrack now sends it straight to the Profile screen.
symptoms: Where is scan history
There is no History tab
/history just opens Profile
How do I see my previous scans
entries.rootCause: The standalone /history route was replaced by a redirect to /profile; ProfilePage renders the 'Recent Scans' section fed by GET /api/scans. Bottom nav exposes HOME / SCAN / PROFILE only.

evidence.snippet:
{/* Old /history URLs redirect to the new combined profile page. */}
<Route path="/history" element={<Navigate to="/profile" replace />} />

{/* ── Recent scans ── */}

Recent Scans
'/profile':          { title: 'Profile',             sub: 'Account & history' },

entries.question: My Recent Scans list only shows 5 scans — where are the rest?
entries.answer:
Nothing is missing. Recent Scans shows the 5 newest by default and hides the rest behind a button.

1. Scroll to the bottom of the Recent Scans list.
2. Tap "Show all N scans" (N is your real total).
3. The full list appears; tap "Show less" to collapse it back to 5.

The button only appears when you have more than 5 scans. There is no page-by-page paging — once expanded, every scan you are allowed to see is on the screen at once, newest first.
symptoms: Only 5 scans showing
Where is the rest of my history
Show all scans button
History list is cut off
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage slices the /api/scans response to 5 unless showAllScans is toggled; the server route returns the complete list with no limit or offset parameter.

evidence.snippet:
// Show the 5 most recent by default; "Show all" reveals the full history.
const recent  = useMemo(() => (showAllScans ? scans : scans.slice(0, 5)), [scans, showAllScans]);

entries.question: What do the numbers on each row of Recent Scans mean?
entries.answer:
Each row summarises one scan:

• The picture on the left is the original photo you took of that rack. If no photo was kept, you get a terminal icon instead.
• The bold code (for example RK-4F2A9C) is the rack ID — it is the scan's permanent address.
• The line under it reads "N dev · N units · N ports":
  – dev = how many devices RackTrack found in the rack.
  – units = how many rack units it mapped.
  – ports = how many port identifications have been recorded for that rack so far. This one grows every time you identify another port, so an older scan can show more ports than a newer one.
• On the right is how long ago the scan was taken — "just now", "12m ago", "5h ago", "3d ago", "2w ago", "4mo ago".

There is no search box and no sort control: the list is always newest first.
symptoms: What does 3 dev 12 units 8 ports mean
Port count on history row keeps changing
Can I search my scan history
How is the history list sorted
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage renders rackId, deviceCount, unitCount, portCount and a relative timestamp from /api/scans; portCount is the line count of port_identifications.jsonl, and the server sorts by timestamp descending. No search or sort UI exists.

evidence.snippet:

{s.rackId}

{s.deviceCount} dev · {s.unitCount} units · {s.portCount} port{s.portCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}

entries.question: How do I reopen a scan I did last week and get back to its results?
entries.answer:
Tap it — that is all.

1. PROFILE tab → Recent Scans.
2. Tap the row for the rack you want (tap "Show all N scans" first if it is older than the last five).
3. RackTrack reloads that scan and drops you on its results screen, with the same Overview / Ports / Topology / Network / Switches tabs as when you first scanned it.

The address it opens is /results/<rack ID>, so you can also type or bookmark that directly — for example /results/RK-4F2A9C — and land straight on the scan without going through Profile. Reopening a scan does not re-run the analysis and does not use your camera.
symptoms: How do I open an old scan
Reopen previous result
Bookmark a scan
Get back to last week's rack
entries.rootCause: openScan() fetches /api/scan/<rackId>/report?format=json and navigates to /results/<rackId> with the result preloaded in router state; the /results/:rackId route is deep-linkable and re-fetches via /api/scan/:rackId when opened cold.

entries.question: I tapped an old scan and a red message appeared saying the scan was not found.
entries.answer:
That scan's data is no longer on the server, so RackTrack cannot rebuild the results screen. The message is "Scan <rack ID> not found" and it appears as a red banner just under the Recent Scans heading.

What to do:
1. Pull the app back to Profile and try another scan — if the others open, only that one rack's data is gone.
2. Take a fresh photo of that rack from the SCAN tab. You will get results again (a new rack ID if the photo is new).
3. If several old scans fail the same way, tell your organization admin — something removed rack folders on the server.

If instead you opened a /results/<rack ID> link and the rack no longer exists, RackTrack quietly drops it from the app's local list and sends you to the Scan screen rather than showing an error.
symptoms: Scan RK-... not found
Red banner on Profile when opening a scan
Old scan won't open
Tapping a history row does nothing / bounces to Scan
entries.rootCause: buildScanReportData throws 'Scan <rackId> not found' when scan_meta.json is missing, and the report route converts any throw into a 404; ProfilePage surfaces the message in scansError. ResultsPage handles a cold-link 404 by pruning the local cache and redirecting to /scan.

entries.question: My Recent Scans says "No scans yet." but I have definitely scanned racks.
entries.answer:
"No scans yet." plus a "Start your first scan" button means the server returned an empty list for the account you are signed in as. Work through these in order:

1. Check who you are signed in as — your username and email are at the top of the same Profile screen. A second account (or a re-signup) starts with an empty history.
2. Check whether you were moved to a different Site. Your history is the racks you claimed while in your current Site; if an admin moved you, the older scans stay with the old Site.
3. Remember that you only see scans you ran yourself. A colleague's scan of the same rack does not appear in your list.
4. If none of that fits, ask your organization admin — they can see every scan from every Site in the organization and can confirm the scan still exists.

A red error banner instead of "No scans yet." means a loading failure, not an empty history — pull the screen again.
symptoms: No scans yet
History empty after signing in
Start your first scan button but I already scanned
My scans disappeared
entries.rootCause: For a member, /api/scans intersects the outputs folders with tenantUserRackIds(tenant_id, user_id) — racks claimed in the CURRENT Site by THIS user. A different account, a Site move, or a colleague's claim all yield an empty set. The empty state renders only when there is no error.

entries.question: I was moved to a different site and now my old scans are gone from Recent Scans.
entries.answer:
That is expected. Your scan history follows the Site you are in, not just your login.

RackTrack records each scan as "this Site claimed this rack, and this person did it". When an admin changes your Site, your list is rebuilt from the racks claimed in the new Site, so scans you ran under the old Site stop showing for you.

What to do:
1. Ask your organization admin to look the rack up — an org admin sees every scan from every Site in the organization, including your old ones.
2. If you need the rack on-screen right now and you know its rack ID (RK-…), ask the admin for it; but note the app will still refuse to open a rack that belongs to a Site you are no longer in.
3. If you need the rack in your new Site's history, simply scan it again from your new Site.

Nothing was deleted — the old scans are still on the server under the old Site.
symptoms: History emptied after being moved to another site
Scans vanished after admin changed my site
Rack not found after site change
Lost my history but colleague still sees it
entries.rootCause: PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId can set users.tenant_id. /api/scans for a member queries rack_owners by (tenant_id, created_by), and the :rackId guard denies members any rack their current tenant does not own — so a Site move detaches the member from previously claimed racks.

evidence.snippet:
_stmtUserRackIds = db.prepare(
    `SELECT rack_id FROM rack_owners WHERE tenant_id = ? AND created_by = ?`);

entries.question: Can I delete a single scan from my history, or clear the whole list?
entries.answer:
No. There is no delete on a scan.

Recent Scans rows do one thing when you tap them: open the scan. There is no swipe-to-delete, no long-press menu, and no "Clear history" button anywhere in the app, and the server has no endpoint that removes a scan.

If a scan must go away:
• Ask your organization admin. Removal is a server-side, platform-level clean-up — not something you can do from the phone.
• Note that a scan is not deleted just because a person is removed from the organization; the scan stays and simply loses the "by <name>" credit.

If you only want the scan out of your way, remember the list is newest-first — a fresh scan pushes older ones down.
symptoms: How do I delete a scan
Clear scan history
Remove a rack from Recent Scans
Swipe to delete does nothing
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage's scan rows expose only an open action, /api/scans is read-only, and no DELETE route exists for a scan or rack. The only deletes that touch rack ownership are org removal and member removal in auth.js.

entries.question: Do my past scans expire? How long can I go back and open one?
entries.answer:
There is no expiry date on your scans. A scan you ran stays in Recent Scans and stays openable for as long as it is still claimed by your Site — RackTrack does not age scans out after a month, a quarter or a year, and there is no cap on how many you can have.

Two things do make a scan disappear, and neither is a timer on your history:
• The rack stopped being owned by any Site — for example after an organization was removed on the server. Unclaimed rack folders become eligible for a server clean-up.
• You moved to another Site, or you are signed in as a different account. The scan still exists; it is just not yours to list any more.

If an old scan matters for an audit, export it while you can — open it and use the report (HTML / PDF / CSV / JSON), which gives you a copy that does not depend on the server.
symptoms: How long is scan history kept
Do scans get deleted after 30 days
Retention of past scans
Will my old racks disappear
entries.rootCause: Nothing prunes scans by age while a rack_owners row exists; the only scheduled deletion is orphan GC, which targets outputs/RK-* folders with NO rack_owners row and is dry-run unless ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1.

...

entries.question: Can I put two past scans of the same rack side by side to see what changed?
entries.answer:
There is no built-in "compare two scans" view. Every scan is its own permanent page, so compare them by opening both:

• On a laptop or desktop: open /results/<rack ID> for the first scan in one browser tab and the second rack ID in another tab, then flip between them.
• On the phone: open one from Profile → Recent Scans, note what you need, use Back, then open the other.

The side-by-side rack toggle you may have seen is a different feature — it belongs to a two-rack scan group ("Scan two racks") and switches between the two racks of that group, not between two scans taken at different times.

If what you actually want is what changed on a switch over time, use Port history & drift instead — that view is built for before/after and has a change log.
symptoms: Compare two scans
Diff between old and new scan
Side by side past results
What changed since last scan
entries.rootCause: No scan-to-scan diff exists. RackToggle only renders one rack of a multi-rack group at a time; each scan is addressable at /results/:rackId, so the practical workaround is two deep links. Temporal change is covered by the port history/drift view.

entries.question: On a port's History tab, how far back does the "Value at" table and the change log go?
entries.answer:
Open a switch on Port history & drift, tap a port tile, then tap the History tab. You get two blocks:

• "Value at" — the port's state as it was 1h, 3h, 12h, 1d and 1w ago. Five fixed points, nothing longer than a week. If several of those points fall on the same recorded state you will see one row with a label like "1h+" instead of five identical rows — that just means the port has not changed in that whole span.
• "Change log (N)" — the most recent changes for that port, newest first, up to 200 of them. N in the heading is how many are being shown.

The Timeline tab next to it has its own picker: Last 1 Hour, Last 3 Hours, Last 12 Hours, Last 1 Day, Last 1 Week. Again, one week is the longest view.

If you need to prove a change older than that, save the evidence while it is still on screen.
symptoms: Port history only goes back a week
What does 1h+ mean in Value at
Change log cut off
Timeline window options
entries.rootCause: The /history route computes exactly five offsets (1h/3h/12h/1d/1w) and requests eventsForPort with a limit of 200; the client's WINDOW_OPTIONS top out at 1 week and dedupedOffsets collapses identical snapshots into a '<first>+' row.

  { key: '3h',  label: 'Last 3 Hours', sec: 3  * 3600 },
  { key: '12h', label: 'Last 12 Hours',sec: 12 * 3600 },
  { key: '1d',  label: 'Last 1 Day',   sec: 24 * 3600 },
  { key: '1w',  label: 'Last 1 Week',  sec: 7  * 24 * 3600 },
];

entries.question: A port's change log says "No changes recorded yet." even though the port has been monitored for days.
entries.answer:
That is a healthy port, not a broken history.

RackTrack only writes a history entry when something about the port actually changes — link goes up or down, speed changes, the admin state flips, the description or the LLDP neighbour changes. A port that has stayed exactly the same since monitoring began has nothing to log, so the Change log heading shows "Change log (0)" and the message "No changes recorded yet."

How to confirm the port really is being watched:
1. Stay on the port's Specs tab and look at "Last poll" — it should show a recent time.
2. "Last change" tells you when the current state was first recorded.
3. Unplug/replug or shut/no-shut the port if you need to prove logging works; the change appears on the next poll.

If "Last poll" is blank or very old, the problem is polling, not history.
symptoms: No changes recorded yet
Change log 0
Port history empty but port is monitored
Drift log shows nothing
entries.rootCause: port_events rows are written only on a detected diff (writePollTxn compares against the previous snapshot), and snapshots are likewise written only on change — so a stable port legitimately has zero events.

evidence.snippet:

{events.length === 0 ? (
No changes recorded yet.

<KV label="Last poll"     value={device?.last_seen ? fmtAgo(device.last_seen) : '—'} />

entries.question: Admin: how many scans does the Organizations console show me, and can I search or filter them?
entries.answer:
The organization dashboard shows the 40 most recent scans across every Site in your organization, newest first — it is a fixed cap, not a page-1-of-N. The platform owner's own dashboard is capped lower, at the 15 most recent across the whole platform.

Filtering is by click, not by typing — there is no search box:
• Click a person's card to narrow the grid to their scans; the heading changes to "Scans · by <username>".
• Click a Site row to narrow to that Site; the heading becomes "Scans · <site name>".
• Click "Show all" (or the same card again) to clear the filter.

Because the filter is applied in the browser to the 40 rows already loaded, filtering by a person who has not scanned recently can legitimately show "No scans for this selection yet." even though that person has older scans. To reach anything older than the last 40, open it by rack ID at /results/<rack ID>.

Note the totals tile counts every scan ever claimed by your Sites, so it will normally be much larger than 40.
symptoms: Org console only shows 40 scans
No scans for this selection yet but the user has scanned
Can I search scans in the organization console
Scan count doesn't match the grid
entries.rootCause: GET /api/orgs/:orgId/dashboard returns recentScans with LIMIT 40 (owner dashboard LIMIT 15) while totals.scans is a COUNT(*) over rack_owners; OrgConsolePage filters that already-fetched array client-side by user id or site name.

entries.question: Admin: if I remove a member, or the owner removes an organization, what happens to their scan history?
entries.answer:
Two very different outcomes.

Removing a member (DELETE /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId):
• The scans survive. rack_owners.created_by is set to NULL and only the user row is deleted, inside one transaction.
• The racks stay claimed by their Site, so the Site and the organization keep seeing them; in the console's scan grid the attribution line falls back to "—" instead of "by <username>".
• You cannot remove yourself ("You cannot remove your own account"), an owner account, or — unless you are the owner — an org admin.

Removing an organization (owner only, DELETE /api/orgs/:orgId):
• Every rack_owners row for that org's Sites is deleted, along with rack_groups, invites, users and the Sites themselves; audit rows are kept but have their tenant_id nulled.
• The scan folders on disk are NOT deleted by that call — they simply become unowned, which means nobody can list or open them any more, and they then match the orphan sweep (folders with no rack_owners row, older than 14 days by default).
• Export anything you need before deleting an organization; there is no undo.
symptoms: What happens to scans when I remove a user
Scans show by — instead of a name
Deleting an organization removes scan history
Can I recover scans after removing an org
entries.rootCause: member.remove nulls rack_owners.created_by and deletes only the user; org.remove deletes rack_owners/rack_groups/users/tenants for the org, leaving outputs/<rackId>/ folders unreferenced and therefore orphan-GC eligible.

evidence.snippet: {s.by_user ? `by ${s.by_user}` : '—'}{s.site ? ` · ${s.site}` : ''}

entries.question: Owner: what actually deletes old scan folders, and how do I run or preview that clean-up?
entries.answer:
Only orphan GC deletes scan folders, and only unowned ones.

What it targets: directories under outputs/ matching /^RK-[A-F0-9]+$/ that have no row in rack_owners AND whose mtime is older than the retention threshold (default 14 days). Both guards must pass — an owned rack is never touched regardless of age, and a fresh folder is never touched even if its claim row has not committed yet.

How it runs:
• Automatically every 24h from server start, dry-run by default. Set ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1 to make the scheduled sweep actually delete; ORPHAN_GC_RETENTION_DAYS overrides the 14-day threshold (non-numeric falls back to 14). Each sweep logs event orphan_gc.scheduled with counts and up to 5 sample rack IDs.
• On demand: POST /api/admin/orphan-gc/run with body { dryRun, retentionDays }. dryRun defaults to true — you must pass dryRun:false explicitly to delete. The call is audited as orphan_gc.run and gated by AUDIT_ADMINS (if that variable is empty, every authenticated caller passes the check).
• From a shell: node server/lib/orphan_gc.js --dry-run, or --apply [--retention-days N].

Deletion is a recursive rmSync with no archive and no undo. Preview with a dry run and read the returned orphans list before applying.
symptoms: What deletes scan folders
outputs directory growing
How to run orphan GC
Can I recover a deleted rack folder
entries.rootCause: orphan_gc.js is the only code path that removes outputs/RK-*/ directories; it is invoked by a 24h setInterval (dry-run unless ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1), by POST /api/admin/orphan-gc/run (dryRun defaults true, _isAdmin gated by AUDIT_ADMINS), and by its own CLI.

evidence.snippet:
* Two safety belts:
 *   1. We only target folders matching /^RK-[A-F0-9]+$/ — won't touch
 *      anything else under outputs/.
 *   2. `retentionDays` (default 14) — folder must also be older than
 *      this. Stops a race where a fresh scan's folder exists for a
 *      tick before its rack_owners row is committed.

entries.question: Internal: a scan is counted in the organization totals but never appears in Recent Scans — why?
entries.answer:
The two numbers come from different sources and can legitimately disagree.

• Org/owner dashboard totals are a plain COUNT(*) over the rack_owners table — pure database, never looks at disk.
• /api/scans (the Profile Recent Scans list) starts from fs.readdirSync(outputsDir), keeps only names starting with 'RK-', intersects them with the caller's allowed rack set, and then drops any rack whose scan_meta.json cannot be read: `const meta = readMeta(rackId); if (!meta) return null;`. readMeta returns null both when the file is absent and when it is corrupt/truncated (it swallows the JSON parse error by design).

So a rack whose folder was moved, whose volume is not mounted, or whose scan_meta.json was truncated by a crash mid-write disappears from every history list while still being counted in the totals — silently, with no error to the user.

Diagnosis order:
1. ls outputs/<rackId>/ — does the folder exist on this server at all?
2. Is scan_meta.json present and valid JSON? Other flows (e.g. /api/select) can rebuild a missing meta from scan_result.json, but /api/scans itself never heals — it just omits the row.
3. Compare against rack_owners for that rack_id to confirm the claim still exists.

Note the same route also reads device_unit_map.json and port_identifications.jsonl per rack on every call, so a large outputs/ directory makes this endpoint proportionally slower.
symptoms: Scan count higher than the list
Rack counted but not listed
Scan missing from Profile but present in DB
Recent Scans slow to load
entries.rootCause: /api/scans enumerates the filesystem and requires a readable scan_meta.json per rack, while dashboard totals COUNT(*) rack_owners rows; readMeta returns null on both missing and corrupt meta, so such racks are filtered out with no error.

evidence.snippet:
const totals = {
      sites: siteIds.length,
      users: db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM users WHERE organization_id = ?').get(orgId).c,
      scans: db.prepare(`SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM rack_owners WHERE tenant_id IN (${inList})`).get().c,

entries.question: Internal: a user says a "Clear" button wiped their scan history — where is that button?
entries.answer:
It is not reachable. HistoryPage.jsx still exists and is still imported by App.jsx, but no <Route> renders it — /history is a redirect to /profile. Nobody can reach its "Scan history" header, its "Clear" button, or its "No past scans yet." empty state through the app. Treat any report about them as a stale build, a screenshot from an old version, or a URL typed by hand into a dev bundle.

What does still exist is the localStorage key rackTrackHistory:
• ResultsPage appends the current result to it and truncates with history.slice(0, 12) — so at most 12 entries, per browser/device, per WebView, never synced to the server.
• The only live readers/writers left are ResultsPage: it writes on every new result and prunes the entry when a cold /results/<rackId> link 404s.
• Signing out or clearing site data drops it, and it has no effect on Recent Scans, which is served entirely by GET /api/scans.

So: the authoritative history is server-side; rackTrackHistory is a vestigial 12-item local cache. Clearing browser storage never deletes a scan.

Scan history page with a Clear button
No past scans yet message
History differs between phone and laptop
entries.rootCause: HistoryPage is dead code (imported, never routed); the local rackTrackHistory cache is capped at 12 entries and is device-local, while the real history comes from GET /api/scans.

entries.question: Internal: is port history & drift scoped per organization like scan history is?
entries.answer:
No. Scan history is tenant-scoped; port history is not.

server/port_history.js mounts a single guard — router.use('/api/ports', auth.requireAuth) — and nothing below it consults req.user.tenant_id, organization_id or role. GET /api/ports/devices returns every row in monitored_devices, and /api/ports/:deviceId/... resolves the device purely by numeric id, 404ing only when the id does not exist. Compare this with the rack side, where app.param('rackId') denies members any rack their Site does not own.

Consequences to keep in mind when answering tickets:
• Any authenticated user of any organization can list every monitored switch and read its full port history, change log and timeline.
• The manual poll endpoint is likewise open to any authenticated user; the only brake is the per-(user, device) rate limit of 5 polls/minute and the per-device busy guard returning 409.
• Host and SSH port are not exposed to the client (toClientView omits them), so this is a data-visibility issue, not a credential leak.

Do not tell a customer that another organization's switches are hidden from them on this screen. Escalate rather than reassure.
symptoms: I can see a switch that isn't ours
Port history shows switches from another site
Is drift data tenant isolated
Who can trigger a manual poll
entries.rootCause: All /api/ports routes are protected by requireAuth only — no tenant/org/role filter is applied to listDevices() or to per-device lookups, unlike the rack routes which go through app.param('rackId').

evidence.snippet: router.use('/api/ports', auth.requireAuth);
